text:
The Federal Government is considering the introduction of assessment test for Nigerians who obtain degrees from foreign institutions, particularly in African countries.
Acting Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Education, Dr Folake Olatunji-David, disclosed this at the 37th meeting of the National Standing Committee (NSC) on Evaluation of Foreign Qualifications in Abuja on Monday.
Olatunji-David said the assessment test was necessary before their qualifications would be evaluated for mobilisation into the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC).
She said the proposal was aimed at ensuring that foreign qualifications presented by Nigerians reflected genuine learning achievements and met the required academic standards.
She explained that the measure was particularly important given the increasing number of Nigerians studying in foreign higher institutions, especially in West Africa.
“We must ensure that the standard of education in Nigeria is not lowered by allowing all manner of foreign qualifications that are not recognised, to be paraded by Nigerians without the corresponding learning achievement.
“Inasmuch as we want to encourage global socialisation, education, and the rest of them because the world is a global village now, but we want to maintain standard.
“We want to ensure that, yes, for every certificate given, they are earned, and they can produce people that can contribute positively to our national development.
“I therefore invite this committee once again to consider, if necessary, an assessment test before such graduates are evaluated for NYSC,” she said.
Olatunji-David described the committee as central to efforts to safeguard the integrity of Nigeria’s education system by ensuring that only genuine and duly accredited foreign qualifications were recognised.
She expressed concern over the rising cases of forgery of Nigerian and foreign degree certificates, saying the ministry was taking steps to address the menace.
The acting permanent secretary commended members of the committee for decisions reached at their previous meeting, describing them as important steps towards improving the evaluation and accreditation of foreign qualifications.
She said the ministry had recorded progress in confirming the accreditation status of foreign institutions, issuing clearance letters for NYSC mobilisation, authenticating certificates and issuing no-objection letters.
According to her, the ministry also issues eligibility and proficiency letters to Nigerians traveling abroad for employment or further studies.
“Since the beginning of this year, the evaluation of foreign certificates and authentication of Nigerian certificates have been automated and digitalised, making the process seamless.
“The fees accruing are remitted into government accounts, thereby increasing the ministry’s revenue generation,” Olatunji-David said.
She said the committee would deliberate on five key issues, including guidelines for issuing no-objection letters required for registering proposed institutions with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC).
Others, she said, included compliance by foreign-curriculum secondary schools operating in Nigeria with the country’s education policy on public examinations.
She stressed that such schools must prepare their students for examinations conducted by the West African Examinations Council (WAEC), National Examinations Council (NECO), National Business and Technical Examinations Board (NABTEB) or National Board for Arabic and Islamic Studies (NBAIS), as applicable.
According to her, students must sit for at least one of the recognised examinations before graduating from such schools, irrespective of where they intend to pursue higher education.
She said the committee would also consider the recognition of foreign secondary school qualifications, including the Higher School Diploma issued in the United States and Canada, and the Baccalaureate certificates issued by French schools.
She listed other issues for consideration to include establishing mechanisms for monitoring Nigerians studying in African institutions through institutional visits and recognising foreign regulatory bodies responsible for transmitting information on accredited institutions through diplomatic channels.
Earlier, the Director of Education Support Services in the ministry, Mr Gabriel Amudipe, said the committee’s work was critical to improving learning outcomes, institutional performance and quality assurance across the education sector.
Amudipe said the ministry remained committed to evidence-based planning, effective monitoring and transparent evaluation of foreign qualifications.
He urged members to be objective, fair and firm in their deliberations to ensure that genuine qualifications were cleared while cases that fell short of the required standards were appropriately addressed.
“The design and committee on evaluation remains one of the most critical structures for ensuring that our policies, programmes and interventions are achieved.
“Your work directly influence the improvement of learning outcomes, the strengthening of institutional performance, and the advancement of quality assurance mechanism at all levels of education,” Amudipe said. ( NAN )
